sequence_read: A couple’s automatic everyday coordination moves from reciprocal morning habits, to consulting each other before plans, to treating tiny choices as joint decisions. One person’s work problem becomes shared stress, the pressure spills into a frustrated cushion fight, and he leaves while the argument remains unresolved. She later calls from the still-messy room because concern survives the irritation; he answers while unlocking his separate home. The next morning, their coffee-and-ID ritual resumes, proving an established ‘us’ without implying that they already live together or are married.
relationship_turn: Automatic mutual habit becomes shared responsibility, shared responsibility becomes shared stress, stress becomes safe but real friction, physical separation follows, and care crosses that separation before ordinary mutual belonging resumes.
setup_payoff_evidence: Slides 1 and 11 use the same office-cafe geography, wardrobe, coffee, and office ID as a visual bookend.
Slide 4 isolates one troubling document with Zuv; Slide 5 keeps the same document and laptop between both people while mirrored poses show shared stress.
Slide 6 activates the green cushions. Their scattered state persists through Slides 7 and 9, binding the departure and later call to the unresolved evening.
Slides 7 and 8 maintain one outward movement. Slide 10 completes that path at a visibly different door with the same bag, phone, and nighttime state; there is no visual return.

per_slide.observed_image_first_read: Aachu and Zuv walk through an office-cafe lobby while she fixes his lanyard and their hands meet around a takeaway coffee. It reads as a familiar morning routine.
Two friends wait for Zuv’s answer while he pauses them with an open palm and turns to a phone call before agreeing.
The couple treats two tiny green fabric swatches like a serious boardroom decision.
Zuv privately struggles with one work document while Aachu has just noticed his distress from the far side of the room.
The same problem now weighs on both people; they sit apart but mirror each other’s collapsed thinking posture.
The shared pressure has become an irritated cushion fight. The conflict reads as familiar, contained bickering rather than frightening aggression.
Zuv is leaving with his bag while Aachu calls after him from inside the still-disordered room.
Zuv continues away through the corridor while Aachu remains inside, turning back toward the room and fallen cushions.
Aachu sits alone and makes a tense phone call. Her pressed lips preserve irritation while her knitted brows and self-initiated call carry worry.
Zuv answers the call while arriving alone at another home, using a key at a different apartment door.
The next morning, the couple automatically exchanges his forgotten ID and her usual coffee while walking, restoring the mutual habit introduced at the beginning.

weakest_frame.reason: The direction of the coffee handoff is slightly less explicit than Slide 11 because both hands meet around the cup. The lanyard adjustment still makes the automatic shared-habit premise legible.
